Freezr has no internet permission, no account, no ads and no analytics. Your rules, usage and history never leave this device.
What Freezr does with this access
Freezr uses the Android Accessibility API to detect which app is on screen, so it can cover apps you’ve frozen with the freeze screen and send you home.
It reads the name of the app in the foreground to decide whether it’s frozen.
Only if you turn on website or Reels blocking, it reads the address bar of supported browsers and looks for specific on-screen elements in those apps.
Under Strict Mode, it recognises Freezr’s own App info and Accessibility pages in Settings to keep you from switching it off on impulse.
Nothing it sees is stored, logged, shared or sent anywhere. It’s processed in memory and discarded.
Usage access lets Freezr measure how long you use each app today, for daily limits and your insights.
It reads app open/close times from Android’s usage statistics.
Totals are kept on this phone for up to 90 days and then deleted.
Usage data is never shared or uploaded.
Get a heads-up before apps freeze, limit warnings, and an alert if your phone ever turns Freezr off.
“Alarms & reminders” lets freezes start and end on the minute, even when your phone is idle.
Some phones stop apps in the background to save battery. Exclude Freezr from battery optimisation so your rules keep working. It uses almost no battery: it sleeps until an app opens.
Location (for place and Wi-Fi rules) is only requested when you create such a rule. Uninstall protection can be turned on later from Strict Mode.
Pick a few to start. You can change this any time in the Apps tab.
Tips for Xiaomi, Samsung, OPPO, vivo and others
Your phone’s battery manager may stop Freezr. Follow these steps once.
Note: if you Force stop Freezr from Settings, Android disables it until you open it again. No app can prevent that — Freezr will warn you as soon as it can.

string-array.name: oem_steps_xiaomi
string-array.item: Settings → Apps → Manage apps → Freezr → Autostart: turn it on.
Same page → Battery saver → choose “No restrictions”.
Open recent apps, long-press Freezr and tap the lock icon so it isn’t cleared.
Security app → Permissions → Other permissions: allow “Display pop-up windows while running in the background”.

string-array.name: oem_steps_oppo
string-array.item: Settings → Apps → App management → Freezr → Battery usage: allow background activity and auto launch.
Settings → Battery → More settings: turn off “Optimise battery use” for Freezr.
Open recent apps, tap the menu on Freezr’s card and choose “Lock”.

string-array.name: oem_steps_realme
string-array.item: Settings → App management → Freezr → Battery usage: allow “Auto launch” and “Run in background”.
Settings → Battery → turn off battery optimisation for Freezr.
Lock Freezr in recent apps.

string-array.name: oem_steps_vivo
string-array.item: i Manager → App manager → Autostart manager: enable Freezr.
Settings → Battery → High background power consumption: allow Freezr.
Lock Freezr in recent apps (swipe down on its card).

string-array.name: oem_steps_oneplus
string-array.item: Settings → Apps → Freezr → Battery: choose “Unrestricted”.
Settings → Battery → Advanced → turn off “Deep optimisation” or exclude Freezr.
Lock Freezr in recent apps.

string-array.name: oem_steps_samsung
string-array.item: Settings → Apps → Freezr → Battery: choose “Unrestricted”.
Settings → Battery → Background usage limits: make sure Freezr is not in “Sleeping” or “Deep sleeping” apps, and add it to “Never sleeping apps”.
Turn off “Put unused apps to sleep”.

string-array.name: oem_steps_huawei
string-array.item: Settings → Battery → App launch → Freezr: switch to “Manage manually” and enable Auto-launch, Secondary launch and Run in background.
Phone Manager → Protected apps (older EMUI): protect Freezr.
Lock Freezr in recent apps.

string-array.name: oem_steps_other
string-array.item: Settings → Apps → Freezr → Battery: choose “Unrestricted” or “Not optimised”.
Keep the Freezr accessibility service turned on in Settings → Accessibility.
Avoid “Force stop” on Freezr — Android won’t restart it until you open it again.

resources.string: While any freeze is active, Strict Mode stops you from pausing Freezr, ending focus early, editing or disabling schedules, or loosening limits. To change anything you’ll have to unlock it the hard way — that pause is the point. You can always turn Strict Mode off when nothing is frozen.
On · active whenever something is frozen
Request an unlock, wait %1$d minutes, then confirm.
Set a PIN — ideally one someone else chose for you.
PIN set. 5 wrong tries trigger an increasing lockout.
Needs an online account service — not available in this version.
Longer waits work better. Shortening the wait is blocked while Strict Mode is locked.
Wrong PIN. %1$d tries left before a lockout.
Too many tries. Try again after %1$s.
Make your changes now. Strict Mode locks again automatically.
Unlock requested. Still want it when the timer ends?

Partner approval isn’t available in this version.

Optional. Activates Freezr as a device admin (no device policies are used). Android then won’t uninstall Freezr until admin is turned off, and under Strict Mode Freezr steers you away from the screens that would switch it off. This is a self-control feature you choose — you can deactivate it whenever Strict Mode is unlocked.
Freezr uses device admin only as a speed bump against uninstalling it on impulse. It does not use any device policies and cannot lock or wipe your phone.
Makes it harder to uninstall Freezr on impulse. No device policies are used.
Turning this off removes Freezr’s uninstall protection.
Strict Mode is on and a freeze is active. You promised yourself this time — are you sure?
Under Strict Mode, back out of Freezr’s App info, Accessibility and Device admin pages
Do you really need this right now?
If it’s important, you can open this one app briefly. First there’s a %1$d-second pause, then you’ll type a short phrase.
Take a breath. Still need it?
No emergency passes left this week.
Emergency unlock isn’t allowed for this freeze (Strict Mode focus session).

When an app is frozen you can tap “Emergency unlock” on the freeze screen. After a %1$d-second pause and typing a phrase, that one app opens for %2$d minutes. You get %3$d passes per rolling week. For a daily limit, a pass adds %4$d extra minutes instead. Every use is logged and breaks your streak.
Extra minutes for a daily limit
Under Strict Mode only stricter values can be saved.
At 80% and 100% of a daily limit
Shows protection state with a pause button
Apps that can never be frozen
These apps are never frozen, so you can always call, text, use your keyboard and fix your settings. The core safety set can’t be removed.
Debug: are website and in-app rules matching?
Freezr %1$s · all data stays on this device
Freezr works entirely on your phone. It has no internet permission, no account, no ads and no analytics. Nothing is collected by us, because nothing ever leaves your device.

Used to detect which app is in the foreground and to show the freeze screen. If you enable website or Reels blocking, it reads the browser address bar or looks for specific elements in those apps. Under Strict Mode it recognises Freezr’s own pages in Settings. Screen content is processed in memory only and is never stored, logged or transmitted.
Used to calculate per-app screen time for daily limits and insights. Daily totals are stored on the device for up to 90 days.
Freezr lists apps that have a launcher icon so you can choose which to freeze. It does not request access to all installed packages.
Only if you create a place or Wi-Fi rule. Location is used on-device to know whether you are inside a place you defined, or which Wi-Fi network you are on. Location history is not stored.

Your rules and settings, blocked-attempt counts, unlock logs and daily usage totals, in Freezr’s private storage. A Strict Mode PIN is stored only as a salted PBKDF2 hash, encrypted with an Android Keystore key. Data is excluded from backups.
None. Freezr does not share, sell or upload any data, and contains no third-party SDKs that do.
Uninstall Freezr or clear its storage in Android Settings. Records older than 90 days are deleted automatically.
Turn on Usage access to see screen time.
No blocked opens in this period. Nice.

Calculated on this phone from Android usage statistics and Freezr’s local history. “Time saved” assumes about 4 minutes per blocked open. A streak day has no emergency unlocks and no Strict Mode bypasses.
Freeze apps while you’re at a place or connected to a Wi-Fi network, optionally only at certain times.
For example: freeze games at school, or social apps on the office Wi-Fi.
Location permission (“Allow all the time”) is missing, so these rules can’t activate.
This rule will stop freezing apps.
Couldn’t get your location. Check that location is on.
Location is checked on this phone only and never stored or shared.

To freeze apps when you arrive somewhere — even when Freezr isn’t open — Android needs location set to “Allow all the time”. Freezr only checks whether you’re inside the places you defined, on this phone, and never records where you go.

Works in %1$s by reading the address bar, and in supported apps by recognising their screens. Apps change their design often, so this can stop working until the rules file is updated. If a rule doesn’t match, nothing is blocked.
That doesn’t look like a website address.

“Working” means the selector matched at least once since Freezr started. “No match” means it was checked but never matched — the target app may have changed its layout.
